description: A collaborative team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary:
SPACE PIONEERS is an interactive lunar exploration and survival game that transforms children into junior astronauts, allowing them to experience the challenges of establishing a sustainable human presence on the Moon. Instead of simply learning about space through videos or quizzes, players actively explore the lunar surface using a rover, investigate resources, collect and process lunar materials, construct an outpost, and manage its essential systems to keep the crew safe.

Designed for children aged 7–12, the experience combines immersive 3D environments, interactive simulations, guided storytelling, and ASTRO, an AI-powered mission companion, to make complex space concepts engaging and accessible. Each decision has consequences, encouraging curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving.

By turning real-world lunar exploration concepts into a hands-on learning experience, SPACE PIONEERS bridges the gap between classroom knowledge and practical space exploration. It inspires the next generation not just to learn about space, but to think, explore, and solve problems like astronauts.

SPACE PIONEERS: Mission Beyond Earth

1. Project Overview

SPACE PIONEERS: Mission Beyond Earth is an interactive lunar exploration and survival game designed for children aged 7–12. Players take on the role of junior astronauts, exploring the Moon, collecting resources, building a lunar outpost, and learning how humans could sustain life beyond Earth.

The project transforms space science into an engaging, hands-on learning experience through exploration, experimentation, and decision-making.

2. How the Project Works

The game consists of four progressive mission phases:

  • Phase 1 – Explore and Discover: Navigate the lunar surface and discover important locations and resources.
  • Phase 2 – Collect and Process Resources: Gather lunar resources and understand how they can support a future settlement.
  • Phase 3 – Build the Lunar Outpost: Use collected resources to construct essential components of a lunar base.
  • Phase 4 – Test, Survive and Maintain: Test the outpost and manage essential survival requirements.

Throughout the mission, ASTRO, an AI-powered astronaut companion, provides guidance, explanations, and narration to help players progress.

3. Benefits and Educational Value

The game introduces children to space exploration through interactive learning. It helps them:

  • Understand the challenges of exploring and living on the Moon.
  • Learn about lunar resources and their applications.
  • Explore resource management and sustainable habitats.
  • Develop problem-solving, critical-thinking, and decision-making skills.
  • Build curiosity about science, engineering, and space exploration.

4. Intended Impact

Our goal is to make space science more accessible and engaging for young learners. By introducing the challenges of lunar exploration through gameplay, we hope to inspire curiosity about STEM fields and help children understand the importance of innovation, resource efficiency, and sustainable human exploration beyond Earth.

5. Tools and Technologies Used

The project was developed as a browser-based application using:

  • Google AI Studio: Used to create the initial application skeleton, which served as the foundation for our team's further development and customisation of the game.
  • Google Gemini: Integrated to power ASTRO, providing AI-driven guidance and explanations.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript/TypeScript: Used to develop the interface, gameplay logic, and interactive features.
  • 3D Graphics and Simulation Technologies: Used to create the lunar environment and simulate mission activities.
  • Vercel: Used to deploy and host the application.

The project is software-based and does not require specialised physical hardware.

6. Creativity and Innovation

SPACE PIONEERS combines lunar exploration, resource management, survival challenges, and AI-powered guidance into one interactive experience. Instead of simply teaching scientific facts, it allows children to experience the process of exploring an unfamiliar environment, gathering resources, constructing infrastructure, and maintaining a habitat.

ASTRO adds an interactive learning dimension, while the progressive mission structure introduces scientific concepts in an accessible way.

7. Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several factors while developing the project:

  • Target Audience: Age-appropriate gameplay and instructions for children aged 7–12.
  • Scientific Relevance: Activities inspired by real challenges associated with lunar exploration.
  • Usability: A simple and intuitive interface suitable for young players.
  • Educational Value: Meaningful scientific concepts integrated into gameplay.
  • Engagement: Interactive challenges, visual environments, sound effects, and AI-guided narration.
  • Accessibility: Browser-based access without specialised equipment.
  • Feasibility: Software-based simulations to demonstrate lunar mission concepts.

8. Vision

Our goal is not just to teach children about the Moon. It is to give them their first experience of thinking like the people who may one day explore it.
